_meta.indication: In combination with fludarabine as a preparative regimen for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing treosulfan to busulfan, each in combination with fludarabine, as a preparative regimen for allogeneic HSCT; noninferiority margin of 1.3 on the hazard ratio scale, with superiority testing if noninferiority demonstrated.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 to 70 years old with AML in complete remission or MDS, Karnofsky performance status > 60%; 64% had AML.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) within 2 years after transplantation (events: disease relapse, graft failure, or death).
pivotal_trials.n: N = 570 (last analysis of all enrolled/randomized patients)
pivotal_trials.result: Positive on primary endpoint EFS (noninferiority p = 0.0000164 vs efficacy boundary 0.000149); FDA-adjudicated EFS HR 0.65 (95% CI: 0.50, 0.85) in ITT. FDA relied on OS: HR 0.67 (95% CI: 0.51, 0.90) in ITT (no p-value, no prespecified alpha for OS).

key_safety: Fatal regimen-related adverse reactions occurred within 30 days of transplantation in 1.9% of patients on the GRAFAPEX arm (all pulmonary). Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions: musculoskeletal pain (39%), stomatitis (38%), pyrexia (34%), nausea (33%), edema (29%), infection (23%), and vomiting (22%).
target_moa: Treosulfan is an alkylating agent; DNA alkylation is thought to be responsible for its cytotoxic activity, with hematopoietic stem cell depleting, immunosuppressive, and antitumor activity.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: MYELOSUPPRESSION — GRAFAPEX causes severe and prolonged myelosuppression at the recommended dosage; hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is required to prevent potentially fatal complications.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by an advisory committee.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted 4/8/2015 for treosulfan as a conditioning treatment prior to HSCT in malignant and nonmalignant diseases in adults and pediatric patients.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA approved via the traditional pathway based on one adequate and well-controlled trial (MC-FludT.14/L Trial II); treosulfan had orphan drug designation, and the application was approved following a Complete Response Letter issued 7/30/2021.
